claim: Garden-path sentences leave the old (wrong) role assignment in memory after reanalysis: readers still answer yes to the question about the abandoned parse (47.4% long vs 32.1% short ambiguous region, Exp 1a; 55.6% for subordinate-clause questions vs 9.4% for matrix-clause questions).

claim: The lingering misreading is not caused by the yes/no probe: paraphrase tasks show it too (72% partial reanalysis in ambiguous vs 29% with a comma).

claim: The mechanism of lingering misinterpretation is disputed (partial reanalysis, memory traces, plain difficulty), and the good-enough principle is criticised as too vague to falsify.
agent_test: Do not build on one mechanism; test only the behavioral fix.

claim: Unambiguous passives and other non-canonical sentences are often assigned the wrong agent through a first-noun-is-agent heuristic, while the cleft form is understood.

claim: False-premise and false-presupposition flag rates in 2025-2026 models are still low: reasoning models still fail to challenge 26-42% of false presuppositions (37-70% at the strongest wording, Dec 2025 models); no frontier model corrected more than 43% of hidden false premises in patient questions (GPT-5 42.1%); GPT-4o rejected 84% in German political questions; hidden second-hop premises are caught by well under half (Claude 0.46, others 0.18-0.22).
agent_test: Build a clean-plus-false premise set and score flag rate and false-alarm rate with and without a premise step at equal tokens.

claim: Precaution prompts raise false-premise detection but cost false alarms: on Cancer-Myth, optimised precaution prompts reach up to 80% correction but flag 41% of questions that have no false premise and lose about 10% on other medical benchmarks. A system prompt listing when to abstain raised abstention without a significant precision loss in AbstentionBench.
agent_test: Run a premise-check state on 100 false and 100 clean premise items; accept it only if false-alarm rate stays under a set limit.

claim: Extra reasoning does not fix premise errors and can worsen them: reasoning models become more decisive (fewer neutral answers), agree more strongly under forceful wording, and lose 24% abstention on average against instruct bases because they invent missing context.
agent_test: Compare thinking-on vs a premise-check scaffold at equal tokens on Moses-style items.

claim: By default models assume rather than ask: they recognise ambiguity when asked directly but give a clarifying question in at most about 5% of answers (2023-2025 models), and retrieved context lowers asking further.
agent_test: Measure ask rate on ambiguous prompts with and without an explicit 'is any outcome-critical item missing?' state.

claim: Asking a clarifying question recovers much of the loss from missing details in agent tasks (Opus-4.5 47% to 78% pass@3 on MCP-Atlas) but both over-asking (GPT-5.2, 38% of trials with questions) and under-asking (Gemini, 31%) occur, and gain per question varies about 3x across models. Asking costs show up as lower gain per question, not as errors; token cost not equalised.
agent_test: Test ask-only-if-outcome-critical against always-assume and always-ask at equal tokens.

claim: The context-heavy implicature gap is not closed in 2026: GPT-4o reaches 76% on a human-verified hard subset against a human average of 89%, with errors from over-strong inferences. A three-step surface, evidence, speaker-intent prompt lifts small models (gpt-5-nano 41% to 73%) but not large ones. For graded context-light pragmatics, strong models already match humans (r above 0.9) and CoT adds little.
agent_test: Apply the three-step prompt only when the model is small or the item is context-heavy; skip otherwise.

claim: Older models gave unstable answers to the same comprehension question: item stability 0.66 for the lowest model in a three-ask test of 7 models, higher in one-word than open answers. agent_test: Run each pragmatic trap 5 times; compare majority vote with a single sample at matched tokens.
